svg.aria-label: ADR-001: a run emits exactly one record under the versioned schema; the record enters the append only ledger, versioned in the repository; the latest state is regenerated in the same commit; every claim of a result cites run ids from the ledger; training records are public, serving telemetry private
svg.title: ADR-001 — One run, one record: the repository is the source of truth, and claims cite run ids
svg.text: One run, one record: the repository is the source of truth, and every claim of a result cites its run ids
quantum-cortex, original figure for ADR-001. Metrics are a first class value of the project, by design: a run without its committed record does not exist.
A run
a training or an ablation run;
an invalid or an aborted one as well
Exactly one record
under the versioned schema;
an unknown value is null, never invented,
never a zero
The ledger, append only, versioned
the repository is the source of truth of results;
an invalid or aborted run stays in it:
errors are noted, never erased
cites
A claim of a result
a post, an application, the paper: it cites run ids
from the ledger, so that claims and state
cannot diverge
The schema is versioned
a breaking change is a new version of the schema with a migration note, never a silent edit;
a notebook that trains but does not write its record is a failed deliverable
The latest state, in the same commit
regenerated after every run (the last run, the best value per declared benchmark, the running verdicts against the control)
and committed with the ledger line and the state of the code: one commit per run
What a record carries, so that the advancement rule is computable from the ledger
the benchmarks block: the declared capabilities, the perplexity, a standard suite slot; the comparison block: the control run it is read against, the perplexity delta, a verdict per capability;
the same standardisation at serving time, through the telemetry: training ledger and serving telemetry are the two halves of metrics as first class values of the model
Public: the training and ablation records, in this repository
the ledger, the schema, the latest state; a dashboard of its own reads only the ledger and the schema,
through repository relative paths, never an absolute path, never a user name; it references no stream
of the private metrics, and the private dashboard references nothing of the cortex;
no dashboard is committed before the ledger holds enough records to compare
Private: the serving and usage telemetry
when the cortex serves inside an installation, its usage telemetry flows into that user's own
private metrics, like any provider's; usage data never enters the public repository:
two data populations, two dashboards, no shared source

g.text: what is run and what is claimed
